title: Graph Neural Networks for Automatic Sleep Staging
subtitle: M.Sc. Artificial Intelligence — Thesis Proposal, UAA (Approved May 2026)
description: Investigating how functional graph representations and copula functions can improve model generalization across different EEG acquisition setups.

advisors.heading: ADVISED BY
advisors.affiliation: Cuerpo Académico de Probabilidad y Estadística Aplicada, Universidad Autónoma de Aguascalientes
advisors.linkedProject: Registered under institutional research project PIM24-3 — Modelación estadística mediante funciones cópula

connection: This thesis bridges biomedical signal processing with the same statistical rigor applied throughout my software engineering projects — hypothesis testing, cross-validation, and reproducible experimental design.

problem.heading: 01 / THE PROBLEM
problem.description: Current EEG models often overfit to specific physical topologies. They struggle to generalize when facing domain shifts caused by clinical variability:

approach.heading: 02 / THE APPROACH
approach.description: The proposed methodology aims to map physical sensors into a dynamic functional topology, making the GNN less dependent on a fixed spatial layout.
points: Nodes: Channels described by Higuchi Fractal Dimension (HFD)
Edges: Functional connectivity via PLV & PAC
Modeling: Gaussian copulas for nonlinear multivariate dependencies

validation.heading: 03 / THE VALIDATION
validation.description: Planned experimental design to evaluate topology-invariance and model generalization across diverse cohorts:
points: Metrics: LOSO CV, Macro-F1, Cohen's Kappa
